releases.source: Published before this workflow by the old automatic deploy; summarised from git history.
notes: Guided first game and a How to play screen
Play friends online by link, or tap Quick match to meet a stranger
If someone drops out of an online game, a computer finishes it for them after 75 seconds
Daily challenge with a shared leaderboard, and the Market League ladder
Achievements, a stronger Hard computer and new pixel art
Smoother on low-end phones; your saved game survives updates
Fixed: after reloading the page or rejoining an online match, the game could stay stuck on "Connecting to room…", especially on slower phones or when the app was in the background
Clearer group play: the online lobby shows how many of the 4 seats are taken and which are still open, and the menus explain that 2 to 4 people can play together, online or by passing one phone
Behind the scenes: updates now reach players only after a preview and an owner's approval, with automatic checks before and after
A new look on every screen: warm cream market mat, pastel fruit lanes, coin prices and round buttons
A short market opening plays when you open the game (about 2.5 seconds, tap to skip)
A new pixel-art farmer's lorry with a wooden roof and a string of flags, and market stalls with tiled roofs in each player's colour
A Full screen button in Settings and the pause menu (on iPhone, Add to Home Screen gives full screen)
The table is bigger and clearer: rivals sit across from you, one column per fruit, freshness shown by colour, and the farmer's lorry unloads every morning
Pick one of six shopkeepers before the game; each has one perk and no two players share one
New favour cards: Gossip (see tomorrow's walk-ins) and Scout (peek at one of today's). Good Riddance is gone
Market Days and a Closing Day give each game a rhythm, and prices are posted like a real market stall
How to play starts with the big idea and follows one customer's order from start to finish
Easier to read: Trophies, tips, chips and buttons have clearer text and a slightly darker terracotta
Online: undo your buys on your turn, and change your name in the lobby
Rules version 6: update the app to play online (older versions cannot join), and a game in progress from 1.1.1 can't be resumed
How to play is rewritten as seven short cards in the order the game is played, including the phases of a game and of a day
The first-game tips have a Skip tutorial button
Bad Harvest, Hotel Order and Fridge cards now say exactly what they do
In long games with 4 players, a favour card can no longer turn up a third time after the deck runs out
Optional accounts: pick an ID and a password to keep your progress on any device (no email, no password recovery)
43 achievements in ten themes, and every stall colour is free
25 collectible looks: stall roofs, trims and counter props, and hats, faces, neck pieces and badges for your shopkeeper, unlocked by achievements
A Wardrobe in Trophies, the room lobby and the pause menu; rivals online see your look
Online: update the app to play online (older versions cannot join)
Upgrades: you can build one after each Market Day, as the rules say (before, several could be built in one evening)
A mango costs $1 more, and Big Basket's extra piece costs $1 more, for closer games
Your cash and rivals' cash now climb customer by customer during the rush
Prices and the rank badge are easier to read, and event previews read correctly
The privacy policy is now on the site and linked in Settings; the web game can be installed and shares with a preview
Rules version 7: update the app to play online (older versions cannot join), and a game in progress from 1.3.0 can't be resumed
Shopkeepers are closer to fair: Haggler's first sale each day pays $1 more, Big Basket's extra piece costs $2 more, Nest Egg buys first on day 3, Charmer starts with 4 favour cards
Two stalls get one walk-in a day, and quick matches online have no upgrades
The Daily market has a twist that changes through the week
Change your password in Settings; the results screen has a cash chart and a Share button
Taps while buying are no longer dropped, and the set-up screen keeps Start in view
Rules version 8: update the app to play online (older versions cannot join), and a game in progress from 1.4.0 can't be resumed
A new home screen: your shopkeeper stands at their stall, with Dress up (the Wardrobe) and a Create account sign right on it
New game, Continue and Play a friend open a small menu first; New game holds all the set-up in one popup, and Quick match is in the Play a friend menu
Numbers and dollar signs use a rounder font, so 5 is no longer mistaken for S
No rules change: you can still play online with 1.5.0
A new economy: every stall starts with $15 and buys up to 6 pieces a day (Handcart 8)
Customers have a freshness type: Premium wants Fresh only, Everyday Fresh or Okay, Bargain anything. It shows on each customer card
Ten named lorries, with the amounts for 2, 3 and 4 stalls printed on each card; two of the mango lorries arrive green
Event cards rebalanced; Price Controls replaces Minimum Price; the Health Inspector now fines at the start of the day
Computer shops understand all of the above
Rules version 9: update the app to play online (older versions cannot join), and a game in progress from 1.6.0 can't be resumed
A brand-new look, The Great Fruit Exchange: customers are illustrated trading cards, shopkeepers have stall signs, and each day's event arrives as a Gazette front page
Shopkeepers and customers have new names (for example Uncle Benny, Ah Chen, Kiki, Cowboy Jack and Marina Wen); trophies you already earned still count
New fonts and colours on every screen, with larger touch targets on phones and tablets
No rules change: you can still play online with 1.7.0
New in-game layout: your shelf and every customer fit on one screen, no scrolling
Clearer advice after each sale: the real reason a sale was missed, and what would have won a tie
The price hint now counts only buyers who would take your fruit
Juice Bar: see what becomes juice tonight and what it earned overnight; the card has a new tip
Closing Day now clearly says the jam maker pays $1 for each ripe leftover
Smarter computer rivals on Closing Day and at tied prices
Cards share one layout and the opening flows smoothly into the home screen
No rules change: you can still play online with 1.8.0 (update to send daily challenge scores)
A new home screen: the whole market square, and a new opening where the lorry arrives and unloads the menu
One clear, friendly font across the game
At the rush, each customer's card comes to the middle and every stall's offer is flipped over
See every stall's crates round the table while you set prices; your shelf now empties customer by customer
All icons, stalls and the lorry redrawn in the Great Fruit Exchange style
Shopkeepers now wear their unlocks, plus six new ones to earn
No rules change: you can still play online with 1.9.0
New buying order: from Day 2 the poorest stall buys first, then everyone else clockwise
Rules version 10: update the app to play online or send daily scores; unfinished games from 1.10.0 can't be resumed
New compact rules: play with up to 6 stalls, about one customer per stall each day
Meet two new shopkeepers, Pak Din (Shade Cloth) and Farah (Sharp Ears), and seven new event cards
Smaller orders, smaller shelves, $10 to start and cheaper upgrades; ties now go to fresher fruit before the Haggler
Rules version 11: update the app to play online or send daily scores; unfinished games from 1.11.0 can't be resumed
Tidier New game screen: tap a rival stall's tile to change it, or + Add for another
Pick the exact fruit for your crate from your shelf: only crate fruit sells
New pricing: tap a fruit in your crate to price it, and see how many buyers would pay each price
"The Bell" pop-up explains pricing on Day 1; tap i to see it again
Rules version 12: update the app to play online or send daily scores; unfinished games from 1.12 can't be resumed
Events are now a surprise: each morning the news card is drawn face down and turned over that day
Bigger event pictures, new wording with a tagline on every event card, and art for the seven newest events
Pak Din and Farah have their own pictures, and the Wedding Caterer and the Bakery show theirs
The Cold Room upgrade is gone: three upgrades remain
Price reveal cards follow the same order as the rival row
Rules version 13: update the app to play online or send daily scores; unfinished games from 1.13 can't be resumed
Fill your stall: starts empty, shows your whole shelf, and says stall instead of crate
Day 1 opens with a Calm Day card, like every other morning
Play full screen: asked after the opening; on iPhone, how to add the game to your Home Screen
A cleaner event card back
Swipe left or right to choose your shopkeeper; their tagline shows under the card
A simpler New game screen: the full rules are always on
Shopkeeper cards show just the name
